_note: Anomalous dispatch: solar_1 and wind_1 timeseries were silently zeroed during solution parsing (parsing error). gas_cc_1 runs flat at P_max (600 MW) all 24 hours without load-following. load_shedding_MW=0 everywhere. Result: over-supply at off-peak hours, large unserved demand at peak hours, emission cap exceeded, renewable target missed.

power_balance.root_cause: solar_1 and wind_1 dispatch columns are all zeros despite both generators being in the fleet, and gas_cc_1 runs flat at P_max (600 MW) all 24 hours with no load-following. The most likely cause is a solution parsing error: VRE generator columns may have been silently dropped or zeroed during dispatch CSV extraction, and gas_cc_1 commitment may have been read without its dispatch values. The resulting flat 600 MW profile causes over-supply in off-peak hours (t=0-3, t=22-23) and large unserved demand at peak hours (t=4-21, max 408.55 MW at t=17). Other possible causes: unit index mismatch in the .sol file, or a column ordering bug in the CSV writer.

anomalies.message: Reported objective $148,200 does not match recomputed variable cost $300,672 (gas_cc_1 at 600 MW × $20.80/MWh × 24h = $300,672). Discrepancy 103% — the reported objective reflects only partial thermal dispatch from the corrupted solution file (VRE zeroed, load balance not enforced).

Total emissions 5,040 tCO2 exceed the cap of 5,000 tCO2 by 40 tCO2 (0.8%). gas_cc_1 at flat 600 MW for 24h produces 5,040 tCO2. If VRE had been correctly dispatched, thermal output and emissions would have been lower (expected: ~2,752 tCO2 with correct VRE dispatch).

Renewable fraction 0.0% is far below the required target of 60.0%. solar_1 and wind_1 dispatch are both zero across all 24 timesteps due to the parsing error. With correct VRE dispatch, expected renewable fraction is ~62%.

load_shedding_MW=0 at all timesteps, but power balance analysis shows 18 timesteps (t=4–21) with supply < demand (unserved demand max 408.55 MW at t=17). The physical load shortfall is not recorded in the dispatch output — it is implicit in the power balance violation.

all_anomalies: POWER_BALANCE: All 24 timesteps have |supply - demand| > 0.5 MW. 18 timesteps have under-supply (unserved demand, max 408.55 MW at t=17). Root cause: VRE dispatch columns zeroed in parsing.

COST_DISCREPANCY: Reported objective $148,200 vs recomputed $300,672 (103% gap).
EMISSION_CAP_EXCEEDED: 5,040 tCO2 vs 5,000 tCO2 cap (0.8% over). Caused by flat thermal dispatch without VRE offset.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Do not use this solution. Re-parse the solver .sol file with verbose column logging to recover solar_1 and wind_1 dispatch timeseries.
Route to Refiner Agent with OUTPUT_ANOMALY context, trigger: POWER_BALANCE_VIOLATION.

Check dispatch CSV extraction logic: verify all generator columns are written. VRE generators may be missing from the column index if they use always-on commitment (no binary u[g,t] variable) that differs from thermal generators.
Once VRE parsing is fixed and the dispatch is regenerated, emission cap and renewable target violations are expected to resolve automatically.
After fix: re-run check_power_balance.py and validate all 24 timesteps balance within 0.5 MW tolerance before accepting the solution.
